title: Token-rate bisection + regression harness with p95 fingerprinting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create and maintain an automated tokens-per-second benchmarking harness that can detect regressions in throughput (tokens/sec) and p95 latency, and automatically drive a bisection workflow to identify offending commits or configuration changes. The harness will produce a deterministic fingerprint for each model-version + CUDA/kernel config using a curated prompt set that covers cold/warm KV cache states, multi-burst traffic profiles, and long-tail sequence lengths. Key goals: reliable regression alerts (low false positives), reproducible baselines, and integration with canary and CI to prevent performance regressions landing in production.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark runs produce stable tokens/sec and p95 fingerprints for core models (mean relative variance < 4%) across 10 consecutive runs
Automated regression detection (statistical test + CUSUM) triggers when tokens/sec drops > 6% or p95 increases > 15% relative to baseline
Git-bisect automation can narrow regression to a single commit within the last 200 commits for 95% of injected regressions in test harness
Dashboard visualizes model-version baselines, recent runs, and annotated regressions with links to bisect results and candidate commits
Canary integration: failing regression check blocks canary promotion and opens an ENG ticket with diagnostic artifacts
implementation_plan: 1) Define golden prompt set (200 prompts) covering short/long sequences, KV warm/cold, and multi-burst patterns
2) Implement harness runner that reproduces client-side behavior (streaming vs non-streaming) and exports tokens/sec + latency histograms
3) Add statistical fingerprinting (median/p95/histogram deltas) + anomaly detector (CUSUM + bootstrap)
4) Build bisect automation: harness triggers git-bisect with shims to run historical builds (or container images) and aggregate results
5) Integrate with CI and Canary: a) run on release branch pre-merge b) run nightly on master c) block canary promotion on detected regressions
6) Create perf dashboard in Grafana and a summary report template for PRs/incident triage
7) Run pilot on 3 core models (open-llama-13b, redwood-7b, community-ggml) and iterate thresholds
notes: 2026-03-02: Initial spike completed. Proved deterministic replay for short sequence prompts using our runtime container images. Observed 3% run-to-run variance on a p3dn-like worker when KV warm (w/o network jitter).

2026-03-05: Decided to use combination of CUSUM + bootstrap confidence intervals for anomaly detection to balance sensitivity vs false positives (proposal in Confluence: /redwood/wiki/Perf/Bisect-Harness).
2026-03-08: Trade-off discussed: running full 200-prompt suite per commit is expensive; we will use a 30-prompt fast probe for CI and the full suite for nightly and release gates.
2026-03-10: Added KV cache warm/cold toggles; observed that some quantized kernels show 8-12% variance in cold-start tokens/sec — flagged for model-onboarding team (ENG-12157).

2026-03-12: Prototype bisect run successfully localized a synthetic throughput regression to a shader-level change in a vendor image. Proof-of-concept PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/212

2026-03-14: Working on Grafana dashboard panels and alert rules. Need final sign-off on thresholds from Runtime and SRE. Blocking: access to archived container images for bisect runner (ticket created, dependency ENG-560890).
